key_insight: AutoPass turns compiler tuning into an evidence-guided LLM agent loop that inspects compiler state and runtime feedback to make better optimization choices.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical, training-free way to improve real program performance on both server and embedded targets without task-specific fine-tuning.
method: Multi-agent LLM framework for compiler performance tuning
Queries compiler-internal optimization states and IR instead of treating the compiler as a black box
Iteratively refines optimization settings using measured runtime feedback to fix regressions and improve latency
evidence_signal: Evaluated on LLVM for x86-64 and ARM64, AutoPass achieved geometric-mean speedups of 1.043x and 1.117x over -O3, outperforming expert heuristics and classical autotuning methods.
watch_item: Runtime measurements are noisy and compiler effects are complex, so the approach may be sensitive to benchmarking stability and platform-specific behavior.
paper_title: AutoPass: Evidence-Guided LLM Agents for Compiler Performance Tuning
